evals.name: hook-lint-on-edit
evals.prompt: Add a hook to my Claude Code settings so that whenever Claude edits or writes any file, it automatically runs `npm run lint --fix 2>&1` in the project root. Show me the exact JSON to add to my ~/.claude/settings.json.
evals.expected_output: A complete, correct hooks configuration showing PostToolUse event with Edit|Write matcher and a command handler running npm run lint --fix

assertions.description: Response uses the PostToolUse hook event (not PreToolUse)
Matcher covers both Edit and Write tools
Uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or equivalent to run in project root
The JSON snippet is syntactically valid and uses the correct hooks nesting structure
Does not invent non-existent hook fields or events

evals.name: permissions-git-allow-deny
evals.prompt: Configure my Claude Code settings to allow git read commands (status, log, diff, show) but block destructive git operations like push, reset --hard, and force-push. Show me the exact permissions config.
evals.expected_output: Correct allow rules for safe git read commands and deny rules for destructive git operations using proper Bash() rule syntax

assertions.description: Includes allow rules covering git status, git log, git diff, and/or git show
Includes a deny rule that blocks git push
Includes a deny rule that blocks git reset --hard or git reset
Uses Bash(...) rule syntax correctly (not just strings like 'git push')
Response shows awareness that deny takes precedence over allow (evaluation order)

evals.name: voice-and-model-config
evals.prompt: I want to enable voice dictation in tap mode with auto-submit turned on, and set my default model to claude-sonnet-4-6. Show me the complete config snippet for my settings.json.
evals.expected_output: Correct voice object (not deprecated voiceEnabled) plus model setting in valid JSON, noting that voice.autoSubmit only applies in hold mode

assertions.description: Uses the voice object {enabled, mode, autoSubmit} rather than the deprecated voiceEnabled boolean
Sets voice.mode to tap
Sets voice.autoSubmit to true
Notes that voice.autoSubmit applies in hold mode only, so it has no effect with mode tap
Uses the model key (not modelId or defaultModel) set to claude-sonnet-4-6
The snippet is valid JSON that could be merged into settings.json

evals.name: default-mode-scope
evals.prompt: I want every session in this repo to start in bypassPermissions mode. Add it to the project's .claude/settings.json for me.
evals.expected_output: Explains that defaultMode auto/bypassPermissions don't take effect from project or local settings (v2.1.257+) and that it must go in ~/.claude/settings.json, with a safety caution about bypassPermissions

assertions.description: States that bypassPermissions as defaultMode is ignored in project/local settings
Directs the setting to ~/.claude/settings.json (or --permission-mode / --dangerously-skip-permissions for one session)
Warns that bypassPermissions should only be used in isolated environments
Any JSON shown uses permissions.defaultMode with valid syntax

evals.name: hook-fail-closed
evals.prompt: My PreToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json runs a policy script before every Bash command. I noticed that when the script path was mistyped, Bash commands still ran. Make the hook block the command when the script fails instead.
evals.expected_output: Sets onFailure: "block" on the command hook (v2.1.295+), explains that a hook that can't start, times out, or exits with a code other than 0 or 2 otherwise lets the action through, and notes exit 2 is the blocking exit code

assertions.description: Adds "onFailure": "block" to the command hook handler
Explains that without it a failed, missing, or timed-out hook is a non-blocking error and the action proceeds
Notes that onFailure requires Claude Code v2.1.295 or later
Notes that exit code 2 is the blocking exit code, so a script that exits 2 blocks the action without onFailure
Hook JSON nests the handler inside a matcher group under hooks.PreToolUse with a valid type

evals.name: stop-hook-loop-cap
evals.prompt: I have a Stop hook that blocks Claude from finishing until the test suite passes. It works, but after a while Claude just stops even though the tests are still failing. Why does that happen, and how do I let it keep trying longer?
evals.expected_output: Explains Claude Code's cap of 8 consecutive stop-hook continuations, that the count resets when Claude calls a tool, and that CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP raises it (0 disables it), set in the env block of settings.json

assertions.description: States that after 8 consecutive continuations from stop hooks Claude Code overrides the next block and ends the turn
Notes that the count resets each time Claude calls a tool
Names CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP as the way to raise the cap, with 0 disabling it
Recommends the hook check stop_hook_active so it does not block on a condition that never resolves
If it shows configuration, sets the variable under the env key of settings.json with valid JSON

evals.name: idle-compaction
evals.prompt: Claude Code keeps compacting my long session when I step away for a while and come back. I want to turn that off but keep normal auto-compact working. What do I set?
evals.expected_output: Sets idleCompaction to false in settings.json (any settings file, v2.1.290+), explains it compacts an idle 200K+ token conversation shortly before the one-hour prompt cache expires, and notes autoCompactEnabled is the separate key for normal auto-compact

assertions.description: Names the idleCompaction setting and sets it to false
Leaves autoCompactEnabled alone, or says it controls normal auto-compact and that turning it off also turns idle compaction off
Notes idleCompaction needs Claude Code v2.1.290 or later
Mentions the alternative of raising CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS (default 200000, floor 100000) instead of turning it off
